media_item.item_title: In the Shadow of Justice: The Confession
media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, multiple trials, exoneration after lengthy imprisonment.
media_item.summary_notes: The Dateline episode covers the complex legal battle of David Camm, a former Indiana trooper, spanning over a decade. Key issues included shifting timelines, disputed forensic evidence (especially blood spatter), and the eventual identification of Charles Boney via DNA found on a sweatshirt at the scene.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Former state trooper wrongfully convicted of murdering his family; convicted twice before being exonerated at third trial after evidence pointing to actual perpetrator admitted. Available via NBC/Peacock.
research_notes_other.research_findings: David Camm, a former Indiana trooper, endured three trials for the murder of his family. Key issues included shifting timelines, disputed forensic evidence (especially blood spatter), and the eventual identification of Charles Boney via DNA found on a sweatshirt at the scene. The Dateline episode likely covers this complex legal battle spanning over a decade. The episode appears titled "In the Shadow of Justice: The Confession", rather than just "The Confession."

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Murder (of wife Kim, son Bradley, daughter Jill in 2000)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: David Camm, a former Indiana trooper, was wrongfully convicted of the murder of his family. He was convicted twice before being acquitted at a third trial in 2013 after evidence pointed to the actual perpetrator. He served 13 years in prison before being exonerated.
contributing_factors_raw: Flawed initial time of death estimate
Tunnel vision ignoring evidence pointing to actual killer (Charles Boney, whose DNA was found on sweatshirt)
